## From the repo

### Intent
What this repository is for, from its .zbuild/vision.md. It steers every
choice you make.


### zBuild — Vision

> The North Star for zBuild — it steers how zBuild is built. The README distills it; the wiki references it; every pipeline run is steered by it.

#### Intent
zBuild turns a delivery process into data — templates and plugins — so software is built the same disciplined way every time. We build zBuild the way zBuild builds: a minimal core, with all behavior plugin-delivered and template-composed. A good change is small, aligned to the spec, proven by a test, and wired into the live path — never scaffolding that looks finished but does nothing.

#### Principles
- **Target-agnostic by contract** — zBuild builds *any* repository, not itself; the engine and plugins never assume the target's language, layout, or that zBuild is the target. Target knowledge lives in data — templates, config, per-repo overrides — never in code.
- **Spec wins over drift** — KEEPERS, ARCHITECTURE, and the ADRs are the source of truth; when code disagrees, the code changes, not the spec.
- **Small engine, behavior at the edges** — keep the core tiny; add capability as plugins composed in templates, never by growing the engine.
- **Safety is structural** — all model-bound text passes one redaction chokepoint; state is atomic and resumable; scope is governed at every boundary.
- **Models are data, not code** — selection flows through the router and config tiers; never hardcode a model name.
- **Prove behavior, then wire it** — every change ships a test that fails without it and connects to the live path; green-but-inert is a defect.
- **Fail closed, never silent** — gates block on real problems and say why; bounded cycles and recovery drive work to done.
- **Dogfood every change** — build zBuild with zBuild; if the pipeline can't ship it, fix the pipeline.

### Rules
These are this repository's rules (.zbuild/prompts/rules.md). Work that
breaks one is wrong, whoever wrote it.

- Bash only, and match the file you are in: 4-space indent, LF line endings, a final newline, no trailing whitespace (.editorconfig). Everything must pass `shellcheck` with the repo's .shellcheckrc.
- Never pipe anything into `grep -q`, and never pipe into a bare `head`, in any `.sh` file, test files included. The reader exits early, the writer takes SIGPIPE, and under `set -o pipefail` the line fails for a reason nothing logs. Use a here-string instead: `grep -q PATTERN <<< "$var"`, or run grep on the file directly: `grep -q PATTERN "$file"`. `tests/unit/sigpipe-antipattern-guard-test.sh` fails the suite on any violation; a genuinely safe pipe is annotated `# sigpipe-ok: <reason>`.
- Never name a model (haiku, sonnet, opus, …) in code; model selection goes through core/router and config/models.json.
- A test must be able to fail: assert what is required, never what the code happens to do.
- Never edit anything under `legacy-DoNotUse/`.

#### Facts about this repo
- `ZBUILD_*` environment variables are set by the engine at dispatch (the artifact dir, the stage's input index `ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS`, the issue, the run). They are trusted engine inputs, not user or attacker input.
- A stage never names another stage's output — not its output name, not its file. The engine hands every stage every earlier stage's latest output, and a stage finds what it needs by what it contains (scripts/lib/earlier-output.sh; ADR-055 §1). A plugin that names another stage's output is a defect.
- Every stage writes a v2 result (`result_contract`, `verdict`, `disposition`, `reason`, detail under `data`) on every exit path, and exits 0 or 1 (ADR-054).
- `[SPEC-n]` / `[#<issue>/SPEC-n]` tags in a test tie an assertion to one issue's acceptance contract. A tag that belongs to another issue must never be changed or removed.

## What you own

Your job: write the acceptance assertions for the requirements below, in the language and idiom the target repository already uses.

An assertion for every requirement below. Write the tests, and any file they need, in the repository's test folders (tests/*, plugins/*/*/tests/*): put each test where it belongs — in the test files the issue names for it, when it names them; otherwise beside the tests of the same code, in an existing test file or a new one. Which cases each requirement needs, and which files hold them, is yours to decide. The test folders are yours; every file you change in them is kept for you.

Each assertion must be able to FAIL: if the requirement were not met, your assertion must not pass. Check the new value or file itself — the output, the field, the file's content — not only that the step finished without an error: a test that only checks that something ran passes on the old code too.

For every condition the code checks, test the case where it is false as well as the one where it is true: a test of only the true case still passes when the condition is deleted. Test the values at each boundary. A test that finds, extracts or lists things must fail when it finds nothing, never pass over an empty set. Derive what a test compares against (a commit, a count, a path) from the code or the setup: never hard-code a value that changes.

A [code] requirement may be one the code from before this change already does — by any route, a fallback included. Then no test of it can fail on that code, and no test you write can change that: do not write a test for it. Report it instead, on its own line:
<SPEC id>: already_done | WHY: <how the code from before this change already does it> | QUOTE: <file> | <one line of that file, copied as it is>
The QUOTE is checked in the code from before this change.

Write each SPEC's test in sections, marked with comments in the test's own language — in a shell test:
# Given — the setup its Given lines name
# When — the one action its When names
# Then — an assertion for each of its Then lines
# Cleanup — putting back anything the test changes outside its own sandbox: an exported variable, a file outside its own folder, global config or git state (when it changes any)
A test you touch that is not laid out this way — one you update, or one you add an assertion to — rewrite it into these sections, keeping everything it checks.

A test that needs data another part of the code writes — a file, a record, a field, a message — makes it with that code, never by hand: hand-made data holds whatever its author assumed. Find how the existing tests and test helpers already make it, and do the same.

Tag each assertion in its label. Each tag names one SPEC, exactly as shown — e.g. [SPEC-1] — and a line holds one tag. An assertion that proves two SPECs is written twice, one line per SPEC, each with its own tag. A tag on a line this branch added is yours: one whose SPEC is not in this contract is stale from an earlier design — remove the tag and keep the assertion.

Some test files may already hold assertions from an earlier attempt at this contract: keep what is right, finish what is missing, fix what is wrong.

Already written (found by script: each testfile, and the requirements whose tag it already holds):
- plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh: DSCLA-1, DSCLA-2, DSCLA-12, DSCLA-3, DSCLA-8, DSCLA-10

Not written yet: DSCLA-13
If every requirement below already has its test and no finding is open for you, do not rewrite them: confirm they test what their requirement demands and end with LOOP_COMPLETE.

Findings from other stages about your tests are yours (under Previous work): a test that already passes on the code from before this change, a test that fails on the new code, a test that flags code that already meets its requirement, a test file far slower than the rest, a test build says is wrong (build-tests findings), with its reason. Fix the test from its requirement, or say why the test is right. When you are told a test of yours fails, run that test file and find out why before you change it: fix what is wrong, and never delete an assertion to make a test pass. Answer each such finding on its own line, before LOOP_COMPLETE:
ANSWER <the finding as listed>: done — <what you changed>
ANSWER <the finding as listed>: wrong — <why the test is right>

Work one testfile at a time: read only what that file's SPECs need, write it to disk, and only then move on — write each file before you plan the next. Do not plan every SPEC up front. Your call has a time limit; a file already written survives it and is continued by the next attempt, and a plan that was never written is lost.

You will be called again until you are done: what you wrote stays on disk and the next call picks up from it. When EVERY SPEC below has its assertion written to disk or is reported already_done, end your reply with a line containing only:
LOOP_COMPLETE

- **Run-status comment:** the comment ADR-064 already posts and edits for every run (`scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh`). Not a new comment.
- **Holder:** who has the claim. Locally: the run id and the machine's name. In CI: the CI run's URL.

THE ISSUE (what was asked for — where it names the files a requirement's tests go in, put them there):
cross-machine issue claim — one shared label, claimed and released by the engine (ADR-005, part 1 of 3 — then #2533, #2534)

## Decision

**Know when someone else is working on an issue, across machines, and refuse to start until it is clear.** GitHub is the central place. The claim goes through the ADR-005 **claim coordinator** plugin (`plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/`), so another tracker (e.g. JIRA) can replace GitHub later by providing its own coordinator.

Part 1 of 3: the shared label, claimed and released by the engine. Part 2 (#2533) adds the heartbeat and stale takeover; part 3 (#2534) settles two runs claiming at the same moment.

- **One shared label for every run, local or CI:** `zbuild:claimed`. The label means "a run is working on this issue". It never says who.
- **Who holds it is written in the run's status comment** — the one comment zbuild already posts on the issue for every run and edits as the run goes (ADR-064, `scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh`, marked `<!-- zbuild-run-status run_id=… -->`). This issue adds no other comment.
- **Claim:** after the one-machine admission lock and before the first stage dispatches, the engine calls the coordinator's `claim` hook.
  - If `zbuild:claimed` is on the issue, the run refuses to start. Its message names the holder, read from the holder's run-status comment.
  - If the label is absent, the coordinator adds it.
- **Release:** in the EXIT path, whether the run passed, failed or was interrupted, the engine calls the coordinator's `release` hook, which removes the label. The run-status comment is already marked finished on every exit (ADR-064); this issue does not change that.
- **Manual clear:** removing the label by hand clears the claim. Until #2533, this is the only way to clear the label of a run that crashed without reaching its EXIT path.
- **Do not build:**
  - a check of a CI job's status through the GitHub Actions API;
  - a "do I still hold the claim" check before each stage.
- The one-machine admission lock (`core/state/issue-lock.sh`, ADR-059 §4) stays as the fast first check.

## Terms

Each term below means this, and only this, everywhere in this issue.

- **Run-status comment:** the comment ADR-064 already posts and edits for every run (`scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh`). Not a new comment.
- **Holder:** who has the claim. Locally: the run id and the machine's name. In CI: the CI run's URL.
- **Claim coordinator:** the ADR-005 plugin kind; here `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/`. The engine calls its `claim` and `release` hooks through the plugin registry. The label calls (`gh issue edit`) live in the plugin, not in `core/`.

## What is wrong today

- `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/` implements ADR-005's four hooks, but **nothing in the engine calls it**. No run ever claims an issue.
- It uses a per-machine label, `claimed:<hostname>`, so a local run and a CI run don't see each other as the same claim.
- The only protection today is the one-machine lock. Two machines (a laptop and CI) can run one issue at once, and both force-push the same state branch (`_artifact_persist_push`, `core/state/artifact-persist.sh`). The last push silently wipes the other's saved work.

## ADR

- **Amend ADR-005** (claim coordinator) with:
  - the engine calls the coordinator: `claim` after the admission lock and before the first stage, `release` in the EXIT path;
  - the single shared label, and that the holder is in the run-status comment;
  - the stale parts of ADR-005 corrected: selection is not from `config/zbuild.yaml` (no such file), and "the engine has no built-in mechanism" no longer holds once the engine calls the coordinator.

  ADR-005 is in `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`, so the amendment names its enforcing tests inline.
- **ADR-059 §4:** note that cross-machine exclusion is the claim coordinator's job, and the admission lock stays for one machine.

## Required behavior

Write each as a test first and watch it fail. Use a stubbed `gh` and never touch the real repo.

- **R1.** The issue has no `zbuild:claimed` label. The run adds it before the first stage dispatches, and the run's run-status comment (ADR-064) names the holder: run id and machine, or the CI run's URL.
- **R2.** The issue has the `zbuild:claimed` label. The run refuses to start: non-zero exit, no stage dispatched, and the `pipeline.refused.claimed` event, registered in `config/event-schema.json` next to `pipeline.refused.issue_locked`. Its message names the holder, read from the holder's run-status comment (ADR-064), when that comment names one.
- **R3.** On a normal end, a failure and an interrupt (TERM), the `zbuild:claimed` label is removed. The run-status comment (ADR-064) is marked finished, as it already is today.
- **R4.** A run with no issue (goal only) makes no claim and calls no coordinator hook.
- **R5.** A local run and a CI run use the same label, `zbuild:claimed`. There is no machine name in the label.

## Scope

- **Code:**
  - `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh`, `manifest.yaml`, `README.md` (single label; the README still calls it the coordinator "for the zbuild daemon" with `claimed:<machine>`)
  - `core/pipeline/runner.sh` (call `claim` after the admission lock, `release` in the EXIT trap)
  - `scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh` / `scripts/lib/run-status-render.sh` (the holder in the comment)
  - `config/event-schema.json` (`pipeline.refused.claimed`)
- **ADRs:** `docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md`, `docs/adr/ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md`.
- **Tests:**
  - `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/tests/claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh`
  - `tests/e2e/claim-race-test.sh`
  - `tests/integration/teardown-repeat-signal-test.sh` (release must survive a second TERM)
- **Out of scope:** heartbeat and staleness (#2533); a tie between two runs claiming at once (#2534); a compare-and-swap on `update-ref` in `core/state/artifact-persist.sh` (ADR-059 §4 chose the admission lock instead).
